script runs ~254s against a 150s plan (x1.69); re-cut it

why: an editorial page: one piece of work, the plan, sits half written in a held slot at the centre; a small paper slip slides in at the edge carrying Quick question?; it is answered, and the page's time strip runs on to lunch while the plan stays exactly as it was
a two-column ledger is ruled onto the page beside the slot, headed visible and hidden; one small accent unit drops into visible on minute, the hidden column stays empty and waiting
the held slot swaps: the plan slides out and the question slides in; on switch cost, the first unit is stamped into the hidden column and lettered; the visible column is unchanged

the plan slides back into the slot greyed and out of register; a small search mark moves over its lines until it finds where you were; a second, longer unit is stamped into the hidden column, lettered resumption lag
a faint ghost of the message slip stays printed over the corner of the plan; a third, pale unit is stamped into the hidden column, lettered attention residue
the slot flickers between the plan and the message several times, never holding both; each flick stamps a small unit into the hidden column
the finished ledger for one question rests: one small unit under visible, the stamped units under hidden; the two column heads take the accent in turn
the page becomes the morning as a grid of time units; the first question stamps one accent unit and, beside it, a short run of ink units for getting back in; a small margin note reads varies
the stamps speed up question by question, each one accent unit followed by its ink run; the grid fills from the top while the plan's own units, the real work, barely advance
the same grid: the plan's units now sit scattered in small pieces between the question runs, none of them joined
the hidden runs compress as the worker races, but their stamps relabel one by one from time to stress; the hidden column keeps its height

the spread turns like a magazine page: on the left the asker's page holds one small accent unit and their work moves a step on unstuck; on the right the interrupted page holds the whole hidden pile; a thin line carries the message across
the morning grid with all five slips gathered at one slot at its edge; both column heads, visible and hidden, carry a question mark; nothing moves through the pause

the five slips slide into one batch slot; the visible units stay exactly as they were; the five hidden runs collapse into a single run and the plan's scattered units rejoin into one long block; each slip gets a small tick as answered
the morning layout becomes the habits' board; a first label, batch, pins to the batch slot on its word, and agreed times marks two set points on the time strip
a block of the morning grid is shaded as focus time with a narrow open lane at its edge for urgent; the shading thins on faded, then is re-inked on keep it up
callback to b04: before the plan leaves the slot, a small note is clipped to it reading where you are and what comes next; the ghost of the message over the plan fades on residue
the hook's page returns from the same angle: the slips stack in the batch slot, the hidden column holds one short run, and the plan in the held slot is now visibly further written
a new slip, Quick question?, hovers at the edge of the page; on batch it the slip settles into the batch slot instead of the held slot, and the plan stays in place
